title: Object Lifetime and Garbage Collection
learningObjectives: Explain the main concept in this lesson.
Identify how references, state, or lifetime affect behavior.
Trace an example and predict its result.
Choose an appropriate practice for a simple scenario.

understand.concept: Object lifetime is the period during which data remains valid or available. Some languages use explicit allocation and deallocation; others use automatic memory management such as garbage collection. Garbage collection can reclaim unreachable managed objects but does not guarantee immediate cleanup of external resources.
understand.whyItMatters: Lifetime and cleanup knowledge helps avoid leaks, invalid access, and reliance on unpredictable timing.
understand.analogy: Borrowing a tool illustrates lifetime, but automatic memory reclamation is not the same as returning a tool.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy simplifies software rules; language and runtime behavior may differ.

explain.narrative: Identify the data or resource, who can access it, and how it changes or remains available. Trace the example, and consider what happens after a function returns or when an error interrupts normal flow. Use language-specific lifecycle and ownership rules for real implementations.
